brihadeeswarar_temple.name: Brihadeeswarar Temple
brihadeeswarar_temple.short_description: A magnificent Shiva temple built by Raja Raja Chola I, famous for its towering vimana and the fact that its shadow never falls on the ground at noon.
interesting_facts: The Kumbam (apex stone) weighs 80 tonnes and was carved from a single rock
It is one of the few temples where the shadow of the main tower does not fall on the ground at noon
Built entirely without the use of any binding material—stones were interlocked

hampi_virupaksha.name: Virupaksha Temple
hampi_virupaksha.short_description: The oldest functioning temple in India, dedicated to Lord Shiva, located on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.
interesting_facts: It has been continuously worshipped for over 1,300 years
The temple's main tower is 160 feet tall
It survived the destruction of Hampi by Mughal forces in 1565 CE

konark_sun_temple.name: Konark Sun Temple
konark_sun_temple.short_description: A massive temple designed as a giant chariot of the Sun God, with intricately carved stone wheels, horses, and mythological figures.
interesting_facts: The temple is shaped like a chariot with 24 exquisitely carved wheels
Each wheel is a sundial that can accurately tell time
The main sanctum was originally 229 feet tall but collapsed

mahabalipuram_shore_temple.name: Shore Temple
mahabalipuram_shore_temple.short_description: A structural temple built on the shores of the Bay of Bengal, made of granite blocks, symbolizing the Pallava dynasty's architectural brilliance.
interesting_facts: It is one of the oldest structural (not rock-cut) temples in South India
It has survived centuries of sea erosion and cyclones
It served as a lighthouse for sailors in ancient times

qutub_minar.name: Qutub Minar
qutub_minar.short_description: A 73-meter tall victory tower, the tallest brick minaret in the world, marking the beginning of Indo-Islamic architecture in India.
interesting_facts: It has 379 steps and is 72.5 meters tall
The first three stories are made of red sandstone, the fourth and fifth of marble
It survived multiple earthquakes and was repaired several times

taj_mahal.name: Taj Mahal
taj_mahal.short_description: An ivory-white marble mausoleum built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal, considered the finest example of Mughal architecture.
interesting_facts: It took 22 years and 20,000 workers to complete
The four minarets are tilted slightly outward to protect the main tomb in case of collapse
The marble changes color throughout the day — pink at dawn, white at noon, golden at sunset

red_fort.name: Red Fort
red_fort.short_description: The main residence of Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years, built by Shah Jahan, and the site where India's Independence Day speech is delivered every year.
interesting_facts: Its walls are 2.5 km long and range from 16 to 33 meters high
The Prime Minister of India hoists the national flag here every Independence Day
It originally had a water channel called 'Nahr-i-Bihisht' (Stream of Paradise)

ajanta_caves.name: Ajanta Caves
ajanta_caves.short_description: 30 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments featuring some of the finest ancient Indian art, including elaborate frescoes and sculptures.
interesting_facts: The caves were accidentally rediscovered in 1819 by a British officer hunting tigers
The paintings use natural pigments that have survived 2,000 years
The caves served as monasteries and prayer halls for Buddhist monks

ellora_caves.name: Ellora Caves
ellora_caves.short_description: A complex of 34 monasteries and temples representing Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain faiths, showcasing the spirit of religious tolerance in ancient India.
interesting_facts: The Kailasa Temple was carved top-down from a single rock
It would have taken 7,000 workers and 150 years to complete
The caves represent all three major Indian religions side by side

khajuraho_temples.name: Khajuraho Temples
khajuraho_temples.short_description: A group of Hindu and Jain temples famous for their intricate nagara-style architecture and erotic sculptures that depict various aspects of life in medieval India.
interesting_facts: Only 20 of the original 85 temples have survived
The sculptures depict 4 goals of Hindu life: Dharma, Artha, Kama, Moksha
The temples were forgotten for centuries until rediscovered in 1838

hawa_mahal.name: Hawa Mahal
hawa_mahal.short_description: The 'Palace of Winds', a stunning pink sandstone structure with 953 small windows designed to allow royal women to observe street festivals unseen.
interesting_facts: It has 953 jharokhas (small windows) arranged in a honeycomb pattern
The windows create a natural air-conditioning effect
It was designed to look like the crown of Lord Krishna

sun_temple_modhera.name: Sun Temple, Modhera
sun_temple_modhera.short_description: A stunning temple dedicated to the Sun God, known for its intricate carvings and the fact that the sun's rays illuminate the deity on specific days.
interesting_facts: It is designed so that the first rays of the sun fall on the deity during equinoxes
The stepwell (Surya Kund) in front has 108 shrines
It was built before the more famous Konark Sun Temple

mahabodhi_temple.name: Mahabodhi Temple
mahabodhi_temple.short_description: The holiest site in Buddhism, marking the location where Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment and became the Buddha.
interesting_facts: The Bodhi tree here is a direct descendant of the original tree under which Buddha attained enlightenment
Emperor Ashoka built the first temple here in the 3rd century BCE
The current temple structure dates from the 5th-6th century CE

golden_temple.name: Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib)
golden_temple.short_description: The holiest Sikh gurdwara, known for its stunning gold-covered dome, serving free meals to over 100,000 visitors daily regardless of religion.
interesting_facts: The temple serves free meals (langar) to over 100,000 people every day
The upper floors are covered with 750 kg of pure gold
It has four entrances, symbolizing openness to people from all four directions

victoria_memorial.name: Victoria Memorial
victoria_memorial.short_description: A grand white marble building dedicated to Queen Victoria, now a museum with a vast collection of British-era artifacts and paintings.
interesting_facts: Made of the same marble used in the Taj Mahal (Makrana marble)
It houses the largest collection of British-era paintings in India
The Angel of Victory on top rotates with the wind
